## Role in the Model

This page owns the material and fabrication CAPEX of a central offshore platform. The calculation is common to the electricity-export and centralised-hydrogen architectures: architecture-specific equipment determines the hosted mass, and this page converts that physical requirement into the platform structure, its support structure and their cost.

The calculation is a mass chain. Hosted-equipment mass sets the topside mass; the topside mass sets the jacket and pile masses; each mass is multiplied by a unit cost for its own scope. The same masses are passed to [Platform and Substation Installation](../offshore_installation/platform_and_substation_installation.qmd) for lift screening.

## Cost Boundary

| Physical scope | Treatment | Cost owner |
|---|---|---|
| Topside structural steel and structural outfitting | Included | **This page** |
| Onshore yard integration of hosted equipment into the topside | Included | **This page** |
| Jacket or other support structure | Included | **This page** |
| Foundation piles | Included | **This page** |
| HVDC converter equipment | Excluded | [HVDC Converter Stations](../electrical_infra/hvdc_converter_stations.qmd) |
| Electrolyser transformers and rectifiers | Excluded | [Electrolyser Power Electronics](../hydrogen_production/elx_power_electronics.qmd) |
| PEM stacks and non-electrical balance of plant | Excluded | [PEM Electrolyser Stack](../hydrogen_production/stack.qmd) and [Balance of Plant](../hydrogen_production/balance_of_plant.qmd) |
| Hydrogen compression equipment | Excluded | [Compressor](../hydrogen_infra/compressor.qmd) |
| Transport, offshore installation, offshore hook-up and commissioning | Excluded | [Platform and Substation Installation](../offshore_installation/platform_and_substation_installation.qmd) |
| Engineering, development, insurance and owner contingency | Excluded | Not currently modelled |

Equipment cost and equipment mass have different owners. The component pages book the equipment CAPEX and provide the equipment mass required for platform sizing. This page uses the equipment mass only to size the structure and to cost yard integration; it never applies a structural fabrication rate to equipment mass. Onshore yard integration covers placing, fixing, connecting and testing the hosted equipment in the topside before sail-away; offshore hook-up and commissioning remain with the installation page.

## Architecture Inputs

| Architecture | Platform requirement | Upstream mass basis |
|---|---|---|
| Electricity export | Central AC-collection and HVDC-converter platform | Offshore converter and collection equipment |
| Centralised hydrogen | One integrated AC-collection and electrolysis platform | Power electronics, stacks, balance of plant, compression and shared platform equipment |
| Decentralised hydrogen | No central offshore platform in the current architecture | Not applicable |

The architecture pages determine whether a central platform is present. The relevant component pages determine the hosted-equipment inventory and mass. This page receives those results; it does not recreate architecture-specific equipment models.

## Model Inputs

### Scenario and Upstream Inputs

| Parameter | Symbol | Unit | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Number of central platforms | $N_{\mathrm{plat}}$ | count | Scenario input; the capacity and multiplicity rule is unresolved (DEC-0007) |
| Topside lift modules per platform | $N_{\mathrm{mod}}$ | lift/platform | Scenario execution input, shared with the installation page |
| Hosted mass of equipment item $k$ per platform | $m_{\mathrm{eq},k}$ | t | Derived result of the owning component page; supplied as a scenario list until those pages emit mass |
| Rated power received by the platform | $P_{\mathrm{plat}}$ | kW | Scenario input; used only for the specific-cost metric |

The hosted-equipment list must name each item and its owning page so that shared auxiliaries, buildings and equipment are neither omitted nor counted twice. No component page currently provides equipment mass, so the list is unresolved for every architecture.

### Mass Relationships

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Kind and source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Topside structural and outfitting mass per tonne of hosted equipment | $k_{\mathrm{str}}$ | {{< var platform-structural-mass-ratio >}} | Modelling assumption; evidence required |
| Jacket mass per tonne of complete topside | $k_J$ | {{< var platform-jacket-topside-mass-ratio >}} | Sourced curve fit [@orbitSource2026] |
| Pile-mass coefficient | $a_P$ | {{< var platform-pile-mass-coefficient >}} | Sourced curve fit [@orbitSource2026] |
| Pile-mass exponent | $b_P$ | {{< var platform-pile-mass-exponent >}} | Sourced curve fit [@orbitSource2026] |

$k_{\mathrm{str}}$ represents the deck steel, primary and secondary structure, modules, buildings, cladding and structural outfitting that surround the hosted equipment. It must be sourced from published topside dry-weight breakdowns that separate equipment from structure; no such breakdown is adopted yet.

$k_J$, $a_P$ and $b_P$ are the substructure and pile relationships in ORBIT's offshore-substation design module, where the substructure mass is $0.4$ times the complete topside mass and the pile mass is $8\,m_J^{0.5574}$ with both masses in tonnes [@orbitSource2026]. ORBIT documents them as curve fits without identifying the underlying data set [@orbitSource2026]. They are adopted as top-down relationships because they are the only public mass chain found that links topside mass to jacket and pile mass. Their implicit basis is a crane-installed, piled-jacket HVAC substation; application to HVDC and electrolysis topsides is an extrapolation (see [Limitations](#limitations)).

### Unit Costs

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Kind and scope |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Topside structure fabrication unit cost | $c_{\mathrm{str}}$ | {{< var platform-topside-structure-unit-cost >}} | Assumption; applies to $m_{\mathrm{str}}$ only; evidence required |
| Yard integration unit cost | $c_{\mathrm{int}}$ | {{< var platform-yard-integration-unit-cost >}} | Assumption; applies to $m_{\mathrm{eq}}$; evidence required |
| Jacket fabrication unit cost | $c_J$ | {{< var platform-jacket-unit-cost >}} | Assumption; evidence required |
| Pile fabrication unit cost | $c_P$ | {{< var foundation-fabrication-unit-cost >}} (USD~2022~) | Reused from [Monopile Foundation Mass and Cost](../turbine_system/foundation.qmd) |
| USD escalation 2022 to 2025 | $e_{2022}$ | {{< var financial-usd-escalation-2022-2025 >}} | [Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions](../methodology/financial_and_price_basis.qmd) |
| Exchange rate | $X$ | {{< var financial-usd-per-eur-2025 >}} | [Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions](../methodology/financial_and_price_basis.qmd) |

Piles are open-ended fabricated tubular steel, which is the same product class as a monopile. The monopile fabrication unit cost is therefore reused for piles. The monopile page's transition-piece allowance is not applied, because a pile has no transition piece.

Yard integration is costed per tonne of hosted equipment. This linear form is a modelling assumption: integration work is expected to grow with the quantity of equipment installed, but no public evidence has been found to support a specific relationship. The line is kept separate so that it can be recalibrated or replaced when a supplier breakdown is available.

### Reference Evidence Not Adopted

| Evidence | Value | Reason not adopted |
|---|---:|---|
| ORBIT topside fabrication rate [@orbitSource2026] | {{< var platform-orbit-topside-fabrication-rate >}} | Applied by ORBIT to the complete topside mass including equipment, so its scope overlaps equipment CAPEX booked elsewhere. ORBIT's procurement-year table lists 18,296 USD~2024~/t for the same attribute, so the default's price year is unresolved. |
| ORBIT substructure rate [@orbitSource2026] | {{< var platform-orbit-jacket-rate >}} (USD~2024~) | Candidate for $c_J$. Adoption requires a USD 2024-to-2025 escalation factor and confirmation that the rate is for fabricated jacket steel excluding transport and installation. |

ORBIT sets its substation pile rate to zero, so ORBIT provides no pile cost evidence [@orbitSource2026].

### Validation and Feasibility Evidence (O3 review, 25 September 2026)

| Evidence | Value | Use on this page |
|---|---:|---|
| 2 GW, 525 kV HVDC converter platforms (LanWin) [@offshoreMag2023LanWin] | Topside about 24,000 t; jacket about 10,000 t | Implied jacket-to-topside ratio of about 0.42, close to the adopted $k_J=${{< var platform-jacket-topside-mass-ratio >}}. This supports $k_J$ at 2 GW scale for an HVDC topside; it is a plausibility check, not a calibration, and says nothing about electrolysis topsides |
| Single-lift installation class (Pioneering Spirit) [@allseasPlatformInstallation2026] | Topsides up to 60,000 t; jackets up to 20,000 t | Lift-screen limits for one installation class. With $m_J=k_J m_{\mathrm{top}}$, the jacket limit binds first: a single-lift jacket allows $m_{\mathrm{top}}$ up to about 50,000 t |

No public source was found that gives hosted-equipment masses for MW-scale PEM stacks, electrolyser balance of plant, rectifier transformers or hydrogen compressors on an offshore platform, or a topside dry-weight breakdown separating equipment from structure. Design announcements for offshore electrolysis platforms (for example 100–800 MW concepts) report capacity and volume but not mass. The ABB converter catalogue's 6.2 t for a 10 MW wind converter is recorded on [Power Conversion Equipment](../electrical_infra/power_conversion_equipment.qmd) as context only.

**Proposed multiplicity rule (not adopted).** Choose the smallest $N_{\mathrm{plat}}$ and, for each platform, the smallest $N_{\mathrm{mod}}$ such that $m_{S,\max}$ and $m_J$ each stay within the selected installation class. This keeps $N_{\mathrm{plat}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{mod}}$ explicit scenario inputs checked against documented lift limits, rather than a capacity rule of thumb. It cannot be applied until $m_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $k_{\mathrm{str}}$ exist; the page's single-platform example remains illustrative.

## Calculation

The calculation is performed per platform and multiplied by $N_{\mathrm{plat}}$ at the cost step.

**Step 1: hosted-equipment mass.**

$$
m_{\mathrm{eq}}=\sum_k m_{\mathrm{eq},k}
$$

**Step 2: topside mass.**

$$
m_{\mathrm{str}}=k_{\mathrm{str}}\,m_{\mathrm{eq}},
\qquad
m_{\mathrm{top}}=m_{\mathrm{eq}}+m_{\mathrm{str}}
$$

$m_{\mathrm{top}}$ is the complete topside dry mass in tonnes. It is the quantity that $k_J$ is referenced to.

**Step 3: topside lift modules.**

$$
N_S=N_{\mathrm{plat}}N_{\mathrm{mod}},
\qquad
m_{S,\max}=\frac{m_{\mathrm{top}}}{N_{\mathrm{mod}}}
$$

The topside is assumed to be split into modules of equal mass. $N_{\mathrm{mod}}$ is a discrete input, so a split topside is represented as a step in lift count rather than a smooth mass correction.

**Step 4: jacket and pile masses.**

$$
m_J=k_J\,m_{\mathrm{top}},
\qquad
m_P=a_P\,m_J^{\,b_P}
$$

with $m_J$ and $m_P$ in tonnes. $a_P$ carries the dimension $\mathrm{t}^{1-b_P}$ implied by the source fit.

**Step 5: material and fabrication CAPEX.**

$$
C_{\mathrm{str}}=c_{\mathrm{str}}\,m_{\mathrm{str}},
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}\,m_{\mathrm{eq}},
\qquad
C_J=c_J\,m_J,
\qquad
C_P=\frac{c_P\,e_{2022}}{X}\,m_P
$$

$$
C_{\mathrm{plat}}=N_{\mathrm{plat}}\left(C_{\mathrm{str}}+C_{\mathrm{int}}+C_J+C_P\right)
$$

All terms are in EUR~2025~. $C_P$ is escalated in USD before conversion, following the common price basis.

**Step 6: averaged specific cost.**

$$
c_{\mathrm{plat}}=\frac{C_{\mathrm{plat}}}{P_{\mathrm{plat}}}
$$

$c_{\mathrm{plat}}$ in EUR~2025~/kW is a reporting and comparison metric only. The model uses $C_{\mathrm{plat}}$, which responds to mass, not to rated power.

If any input is unresolved, the corresponding mass or cost is reported as not parameterised rather than zero.

## Model Outputs

| Output | Unit | Downstream use |
|---|---:|---|
| $m_{\mathrm{eq}}$, $m_{\mathrm{str}}$, $m_{\mathrm{top}}$ | t/platform | Mass-balance inspection |
| $m_J$ | t/platform | Jacket lift screen on the installation page |
| $m_P$ | t/platform | Pile handling input for the installation page |
| $N_S$ and $m_{S,\max}$ | count and t | Topside lift count and lift screen on the installation page |
| $C_{\mathrm{str}}$, $C_{\mathrm{int}}$, $C_J$, $C_P$ | EUR~2025~ | Cost breakdown |
| $C_{\mathrm{plat}}$ | EUR~2025~ | Platform supply CAPEX in the project cost summary |
| $c_{\mathrm{plat}}$ | EUR~2025~/kW | Comparison with published platform-inclusive station costs |

The implementation is `model/platforms/platform_material_capex.py`.

This example is set up but reports no numbers. The results will be generated by the model functions above once those inputs exist; they will not be entered by hand.

Two platforms are compared on the same power basis:

- **HVDC converter platform (electricity export).** A {{< var hvdc-link-rated-power >}} AC-collection and HVDC-converter platform, matching the TenneT 2 GW reference system [@tennet2024TwoGWProgram].
- **Electrolysis platform (centralised hydrogen).** One integrated AC-collection and electrolysis platform receiving 2 GW from the collection system. The 2 GW rating is chosen for this example so that both platforms serve the same wind-farm power.

For both cases, $N_{\mathrm{plat}}=1$ and $P_{\mathrm{plat}}=2\times10^{6}$ kW, the rated power received from the collection system.

Once the example can be calculated, it should show whether the electrolysis platform's larger hosted mass produces a materially higher $c_{\mathrm{plat}}$ than the HVDC platform. It should also show whether either topside needs more than one lift module for the selected installation class. The HVDC $c_{\mathrm{plat}}$ can then be compared with the platform-inclusive offshore-station difference recorded as reference evidence on [HVDC Converter Stations](../electrical_infra/hvdc_converter_stations.qmd); that comparison is a plausibility check, not a calibration, because the reference also contains an offshore equipment premium.

## Interface with Installation

This page provides the physical platform definition used by the installation model: $N_{\mathrm{plat}}$, $N_S$, $m_J$, $m_P$ and $m_{S,\max}$. The installation page independently checks transport and lift feasibility and calculates vessel occupation and offshore installation CAPEX.

A material-CAPEX relationship cannot be used as an installation-cost proxy. Likewise, installation vessel selection or duration must not be embedded in the material cost calculated here.

## Limitations {#limitations}

| Limitation | Consequence |
|---|---|
| $k_J$, $a_P$ and $b_P$ are undocumented curve fits for HVAC substations | Jacket and pile mass for large HVDC and electrolysis topsides are extrapolations; their uncertainty is not quantified |
| Jacket mass does not depend on water depth, soil or environmental loads | Depth-driven differences between sites are not captured |
| Topside mass is proportional to equipment mass | Differences in footprint, deck count and layout density between equipment types enter only through $k_{\mathrm{str}}$ |
| Equal topside module split | $m_{S,\max}$ is underestimated when modules are unequal |
| Linear yard-integration cost per tonne of equipment | Integration of dense electrical equipment and of process equipment may differ materially per tonne |
| ORBIT's topside-mass relationship, $3.85$ t/MVA of transformer rating plus 285 t [@orbitSource2026], is not used | It duplicates the equipment-mass ledger and applies only to HVAC transformer platforms |

## Unresolved Evidence

| Required evidence or decision | Consequence while unresolved |
|---|---|
| Architecture-specific hosted-equipment mass inventories (ISS-0052, ISS-0063, ISS-0083) | $m_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and every downstream mass and cost are not calculated |
| Topside dry-weight breakdowns separating equipment from structure and outfitting | $k_{\mathrm{str}}$ is unresolved |
| Fabricated topside-structure unit cost excluding equipment | $C_{\mathrm{str}}$ is unresolved |
| Yard-integration cost evidence | $C_{\mathrm{int}}$ is unresolved |
| Jacket fabrication unit cost, and USD 2024-to-2025 escalation if the ORBIT rate is adopted | $C_J$ is unresolved |
| USD 2022-to-2025 escalation factor | $C_P$ is unresolved |
| Platform capacity and multiplicity rule (DEC-0007) | $N_{\mathrm{plat}}$ remains a scenario input; a lift-limit rule is proposed above for adoption |
| Relationship between calculated mass and installation lift modules | $N_{\mathrm{mod}}$ remains a scenario input with an equal-split assumption |
